story_description: Establish foundational communication layer between Blaze and the Codex app-server daemon, enabling JSON-RPC based interaction for advanced scenarios where the app-server mode provides better session management and event streaming than direct CLI invocation.
task_description: Create CodexAppServerConfig struct and associated configuration management for port allocation, authentication settings, startup parameters, timeout values, and environment variables needed to launch and connect to the Codex app-server daemon.
atom_description: Implement CodexAppServerConfig struct in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerConfig.swift providing strongly-typed configuration for the Codex app-server daemon including port range allocation, authentication token retrieval, startup command arguments, timeout values for connection and health checks, environment variable injection, TLS settings for secure connections, and persistence via UserDefaults with Codable serialization. Configuration validates port ranges, provides sensible defaults, and exposes SwiftUI-bindable properties for the settings UI.
problem_statement: The Codex app-server daemon requires multiple configuration parameters to launch correctly: port number, authentication tokens, environment variables, timeout values, and startup flags. Without centralized configuration management, these settings would be scattered across the codebase, making it difficult to maintain consistency, validate inputs, persist user preferences, and provide a unified settings UI. A dedicated configuration struct ensures type safety, validation, persistence, and clean API boundaries between the manager, adapter, and UI layers.

edge_cases: Edge case 01: Port 0 specified - validate() returns invalidPort(0) since 0 means any available port which conflicts with explicit configuration
Edge case 02: Port 80 specified (privileged) - validate() returns invalidPort(80) since ports below 1024 require root
Edge case 03: portRangeStart greater than portRangeEnd - validate() returns invalidPortRange with swapped values
Edge case 04: portRangeStart equals portRangeEnd - valid, means single port with no fallback
Edge case 05: Empty host string - validate() returns emptyHost error
Edge case 06: Host with invalid characters (spaces, special chars) - validate() returns invalidHostname with offending host
Edge case 07: Host as IP address (127.0.0.1) - valid, hostname regex allows IP format
Edge case 08: tlsEnabled true but tlsCertificatePath nil - valid, uses system default certificates
Edge case 09: tlsEnabled true with nonexistent certificate path - validate() returns tlsCertificateNotFound
Edge case 10: Environment variable with key PATH - validate() returns restrictedEnvironmentVariable(PATH)
Edge case 11: Environment variable with key HOME - validate() returns restrictedEnvironmentVariable(HOME)
Edge case 12: Environment variable with key DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH - validate() returns restrictedEnvironmentVariable to prevent injection
Edge case 13: Negative timeout value - validate() returns invalidTimeout with negative value
Edge case 14: Zero timeout value - validate() returns invalidTimeout since zero means no timeout which is dangerous
Edge case 15: Extremely large timeout (over max) - validate() returns invalidTimeout with clamping suggestion
Edge case 16: maxRestartAttempts of 0 - valid, means no auto-restart
Edge case 17: UserDefaults contains malformed data - load() returns nil, caller uses defaults
Edge case 18: Keychain access denied by user - apiKeyFromKeychain() throws KeychainError.accessDenied
Edge case 19: Keychain item not found - apiKeyFromKeychain() returns nil (not an error)
Edge case 20: Configuration saved with old schema version - load() handles via Codable migration or returns nil
failure_modes: FM-01: Validation errors on save - UI displays all errors, save blocked until resolved
FM-02: UserDefaults write failure - throws error with underlying NSError, UI shows retry option
FM-03: UserDefaults read failure (corruption) - returns nil, caller uses defaults with warning log
FM-04: Keychain access timeout - throws timeout error, UI shows manual API key entry option
FM-05: Keychain access denied - throws access denied error, UI shows system preferences link
FM-06: TLS certificate file not readable - throws file permission error, UI shows path picker
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerConfig.swift and remove any imports from other files. UserDefaults data under key codex.appserver.config can be removed via defaults delete com.blaze.app codex.appserver.config command. No other persistent state affected.

risks: Risk 01: Configuration schema changes require migration logic for existing stored configs
Risk 02: Keychain access may fail silently on first launch before user grants permission
Risk 03: UserDefaults sync timing may cause stale reads on multi-window apps
Risk 04: Validation rules may be too strict and reject valid edge-case configurations
Risk 05: Port range collision with common development tools (webpack, vite) on ports 3000-9000
mitigations: Mitigation 01: Use Codable with explicit CodingKeys and implement init(from:) with fallback defaults for missing keys
Mitigation 02: Catch Keychain errors explicitly and surface to UI with action to open System Preferences
Mitigation 03: Use explicit UserDefaults.synchronize() after save and document single-writer pattern
Mitigation 04: Log validation warnings for borderline cases instead of hard errors where safe
Mitigation 05: Default port range 9100-9199 chosen specifically to avoid common dev server ports
risk_register.blast_radius: Low - configuration is consumed by manager and adapter but failures are localized. Invalid config prevents Codex integration but does not affect Claude or Gemini paths. User can reset to defaults to recover.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If configuration persistence proves problematic, fall back to in-memory defaults only. User would need to reconfigure on each app launch but functionality preserved. Can also hardcode sensible defaults and remove configurability entirely for MVP.
